translationRepairs: Their suppression of treachery and elimination of villains scarcely differed from the methods of Zhi Du and Ning Cheng.
Their suppression of treachery and elimination of villains was rather different from the likes of Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, was it not?

殆與郅、寧之倫異乎 is a rhetorical question of contrast: these officials’ 禁奸除猾 differed from Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, who crushed real villains, whereas the preceding sentences say they flogged the innocent. The original “scarcely differed” inverts that meaning; the proposed rendering is accurate.
When Shusun Hou, an Attendant Secretary in the Palace, was briefly derelict in his inner duty, Ni punished him according to law.
When Shusun Houtou, Palace Minister, was briefly derelict in his inner duty, Ni punished him according to law.
殿中尚書 is the Northern Wei Palace Minister, not an Attendant Secretary, and 叔孫侯頭 is the full personal name Shusun Houtou, confirmed by the next sentence’s 侯頭.
Shusun Hou, an Attendant Secretary in the Palace, had been derelict for a moment in his inner duty; Ni applied the law to restrain him.
Shusun Houtou, Palace Minister, had been derelict for a moment in his inner duty; Ni applied the law to restrain him.
The same office and name errors as the idiomatic line: 殿中尚書 and 侯頭.
Because Yang Ni of northern Pingcheng was a distinguished scholar, Ni recommended him in a memorial.
Because Yang Ni of Beiping was a distinguished scholar, Ni recommended him in a memorial.
北平陽尼 names Yang Ni of Beiping commandery; 北平 is not “northern Pingcheng” (平城).
Because Yang Ni of Pingcheng in the north was learned in scholarship, he submitted a memorial recommending him.
Because Yang Ni of Beiping was learned in scholarship, he submitted a memorial recommending him.
北平 is the commandery Beiping; splitting it as Pingcheng in the north invents 平城.

When he was about to suffer the law, Emperor Xiaowen came to the Taihua Palace to receive him in audience, sent an attendant to proclaim an edict reprimanding him, and then at his home granted him death by strangulation.

When he was about to suffer the law, Emperor Xiaowen came to the Taihua Palace to receive him in audience, sent an attendant to proclaim an edict reprimanding him, and then at his home granted him death.
就家賜盡 is a bestowed death or ordered suicide at home, not specifically strangulation; the idiomatic line already has the broader sense.
During the Zhenjun reign he served as Protector-General of Didao and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang.
During the Zhenjun reign he served as Protector-General of Didao and was enfeoffed as Baron of Anyang.
賜爵安陽男 is the rank nan (baron), not hou (marquis); the biography later uses 侯 for Marquis of Rencheng.
In the Zhenjun era he was Protector-General of Didao and was granted the noble rank of Marquis of Anyang.
In the Zhenjun era he was Protector-General of Didao and was granted the noble rank of Baron of Anyang.
He was thereupon styled the Empress Dowager's maternal uncle to Emperor Xianwen.
He was thereupon styled Emperor Xianwen's maternal uncle.
獻文親舅 means he was styled Emperor Xianwen’s maternal uncle (via Empress Yuan calling him brother), not the empress dowager’s uncle.
When the imperial carriage reached Bingzhou he appointed Hongzhi General-in-Chief of Hexi to campaign against the mountain Hu.
When the imperial carriage reached Bingzhou he appointed Hongzhi commander of Hexi (dujiang) to campaign against the mountain Hu.
河西都將 is a Hexi campaign commander (dujiang), not 大將軍 “General-in-Chief.”
子神 is kinship 子 plus the given name 神, not a binome Zi Shen; the next unit is 長子神.
子 marks “son”; 神 is the personal name.
Shen of Changzi was bold and resourceful from youth and was renowned for spirited valor.
The eldest son, Shen, was bold and resourceful from youth and was renowned for spirited valor.
After 劉氏四子 and 子神, 長子神 is “the eldest son, Shen,” not a native of Changzi county.
He first served as a Central Gentleman of Wuhui.
He first served as a Rapid-as-Tigers Palace Gentleman.
The chapter’s 武卉中郎 is a graphic corruption of 武賁/虎賁中郎. Weishu writes 初為虎賁中郎; Rapid-as-Tigers Palace Gentleman is the correct office, not a title Wuhui.
